transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jonah Mills (Redwood); Liam O'Connor (EdenBank Head of Platform), Maya Chen (Security), Ravi Patel (ML Infra), Sofia Alvarez (PM)

Summary:
Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria, workload sizing, telemetry and most importantly data handling constraints (PII, logs, retention, prompt storage). Customer wants a short pilot that can validate performance, redaction, and auditability on their VPC/private deployment.

Topics covered:
- POC success criteria (latency, quality, cost targets)
- Workload shape and sizing (tokens per request, concurrency, burst behavior)
- Benchmarks (end-to-end, tail latency, stability)
- Data handling: logging, redaction, retention policy, prompt storage, encryption/KMS
- Timeline and responsibilities

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the POC scope end-to-end — success criteria, what you want us to benchmark and especially the data handling constraints. Liam, do you want to kick off with the business drivers?
[00:18] Liam (EdenBank): Yeah thanks Alex. Primary thing for us is to validate we can use an LLM in customer-facing flows without leaking PII into logs or storage. We have to show risk to compliance is zero for the POC. Also performance, obviously — we can't add more than, like, 300ms added latency in the happy path for short responses.
[00:33] Maya (EdenBank Security): To add, SOC2 plus some internal PCI-lite controls apply. We need audit logs, SSO, RBAC and clear data retention windows. For POC we're thinking 30 days of telemetry but minimal retention of prompts themselves, ideally not storing raw prompts unless redacted.
[00:50] Priya (Redwood SE): Totally. On the retention and redaction front we have three levers: runtime-only KV/prefix caching (no persistent prompt store), redaction at ingestion, and post-hoc token-level masking in logs. For private deployment we can turn off persistent prompt storage and only keep ephemeral KV cache.
[01:10] Ravi (EdenBank ML Infra): Quick clarification — when you say KV cache ephemeral, are you talking in-memory on the GPU nodes or on a separate cache layer that might spill to disk? We need to know for our side because DB scans and backups are tightly controlled.
[01:24] Priya (Redwood SE): Good question. For the POC we propose in-memory-only KV cache (per pod) with no persistence. If they want cross-node cache we can do a Redis option but we'd mark that as storing partial states and we'd need encryption at rest and audit policy.
[01:38] Jonah (Redwood): Also note that we support automatic prefix caching so if you have repeated system prompts or standard templates performance improves without storing raw customer messages centrally.
[01:49] Sofia (EdenBank PM): On success criteria: can we draft concrete numbers? Latency SLOs, cost caps, and quality thresholds. For example: p95 end-to-end < 1.2s for average 120-token responses, throughput of 120 rps sustained, and no redaction failures above 0.01% during synthetic runs.
[02:06] Alex (Redwood AE): That's great. We'll propose a matrix: latency (p95), throughput (sustained + burst), correctness/regression (BLEU-ish or custom heuristics on your eval set), plus data safety pass/fail.
[02:18] Maya (EdenBank Security): About the data safety test — we need to run a probe suite that includes seeded PII examples and confirm redaction in both logs and any telemetry dumps. Also audit log integrity checks (who called what and when).
[02:35] Priya (Redwood SE): For the seeded PII tests we can instrument the runtime to redact known patterns (SSNs, emails, credit card numbers) and then run retrieval checks. Note: automatic redaction might have false negatives, we'll capture that in the failure metric.
[02:47] Ravi (EdenBank): What about prompt storage? We have a legal requirement that raw prompts not be stored beyond 7 days for certain jurisdictions. Does Redwood support per-customer retention TTLs?
[02:58] Alex (Redwood AE): Yes, per-tenant TTLs are supported in Dedicated and Private. For hosted customers it's configurable up to your contract. For POC private deployment we can set TTL to 7 days or turn off persistent prompt storage entirely and only keep ephemeral traces for debugging for a short window behind an access control.
[03:14] Maya (EdenBank Security): And encryption — HSM/KMS integration? We need customer-managed keys for at-rest KMS for any persisted telemetry or logs.
[03:22] Priya (Redwood SE): We can integrate with your KMS/HSM for Private deployments, and we support envelope encryption. For the POC we recommend integrating KMS for any S3 or persistent store we use.
[03:33] Liam (EdenBank): On the benchmarking side, our traffic profile is spiky. Peak concurrent users hit around 350 sessions, our average tokens per request is 90 but we have longer flows up to 800 tokens on helpdesk workflows.
[03:48] Priya (Redwood SE): Great — we'll size the workload around three buckets: short (<=128 tokens), medium (129-512), long (513-1024). For the POC we'll run baseline single-node latency tests and a scaled test that simulates your peak concurrency with warm KV cache.
[04:04] Alex (Redwood AE): What's your expected RPS during peak?
[04:07] Ravi (EdenBank): Sustained 120 rps with bursts up to 250 for short windows.
[04:13] Priya (Redwood SE): Okay we'll include steady-state 120 rps and burst tests to 250 for 5-minute windows. We'll measure p50/p95/p99 and token-per-second throughput and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:25] Maya (EdenBank Security): Also want to ensure logs do not capture the full prompt. If redaction fails we need an automated scrub pipeline and an alert. Can Redwood trigger that or do we need to own it?
[04:37] Jonah (Redwood): We can provide a lambda-style scrubber as part of the POC runbook — it can automatically scan new logs, mask detected PII and raise incidents. We'll hand over the scrubber code.
[04:46] Sofia (EdenBank PM): For timeline: what's realistic for a 6-week POC? Week 1: infra setup and smoke test. Week 2-3: load/benchmarks and redaction tests. Week 4: security review and compliance artefacts. Week 5: run full-stress tests and stability. Week 6: wrap-up and decision.
[05:05] Alex (Redwood AE): That aligns with how we've run similar pilots. We can target the week-of-2026-11-23 for the infra deploy and initial smoke.
[05:15] Maya (EdenBank Security): We'll need an NDA in place before we share some of the sample prompts — can you confirm you have an up-to-date NDA?
[05:21] Alex (Redwood AE): Yes, our legal sent an NDA last quarter; I'll resend and confirm sign-off.
[05:27] Ravi (EdenBank): A couple of technical notes — do you support SAML SSO to your console for audit, and is there RBAC per-team?
[05:34] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC are supported in Private. For log access we can restrict to specific service accounts.
[05:41] Maya (EdenBank Security): Also need to confirm immutable audit logs for calls — we want tamper-proof logs for an initial 90-day window.
[05:49] Priya (Redwood SE): We can persist audit logs to your S3 bucket which is versioned and encrypted with your KMS keys — that satisfies immutability and audit trail requirements.
[05:59] Liam (EdenBank): Regarding model selection, we're evaluating a small family of open models for cost reasons. We want to benchmark Redwood's recommended quantized model and also a high-quality unquantized variant to compare latency/quality tradeoffs.
[06:13] Alex (Redwood AE): Perfect. We'll include two model variants in the POC: a quantized low-cost variant and a higher-precision variant. We'll run side-by-side A/B tests and compare token cost, p95 latency and quality on your eval prompts.
[06:26] Sofia (EdenBank PM): For quality thresholds — we're not just measuring BLEU. We'll provide a few hundred labeled prompts with acceptance criteria (correctness + no hallucination on critical fields). Can Redwood run automated scoring and also surface failure examples?
[06:40] Priya (Redwood SE): Yes we'll run automated scoring and produce a failure report with examples. We'll also export the cases for your team to review.
[06:50] Maya (EdenBank Security): One more: we need to understand debugging story without compromising PII. If we turn off persistent prompts how do you troubleshoot reproducing a bug?
[06:59] Jonah (Redwood): Two ways: ephemeral capture with access logs and a masked replay (redacted). Or an opt-in debug mode where prompts are stored encrypted and only accessible via strict approval flow and short TTL. We'll include both options in the runbook.
[07:13] Ravi (EdenBank): Can we get an estimate for the infra footprint for the private pilot? GPUs, memory, disk assumptions?
[07:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Based on your profile (120 rps sustained, 250 burst, token mix), initial estimate: 4x A100-class GPUs for a single availability zone private pool, 512GB total RAM for cache and serving processes, and ephemeral disk for local checkpoints. We'll refine after we get exact token distribution.
[07:36] Liam (EdenBank): That's helpful. Cost-wise what should we budget for the 6-week pilot? (ballpark)
[07:41] Alex (Redwood AE): Ballpark for dedicated private infra + Redwood support for 6 weeks: expect a mix of one-time onboarding and run costs. We'll send a detailed estimate but ballpark $XXk–$YYk — we'll nail down after we set the exact VM/GPU SKUs and hours.
[07:57] Maya (EdenBank Security): For compliance we'll need: SOC2 summary, dataflow diagrams, network port and IP allowlist, and the KMS integration notes.
[08:07] Alex (Redwood AE): We'll compile those into a security pack and send with the SOC2 summary.
[08:12] Sofia (EdenBank PM): Ok to recap next steps?
[08:15] Alex (Redwood AE): Sure. Redwood will: 1) share benchmark template and k6 scripts, 2) send security pack + NDA, 3) propose a pilot infra spec and pricing, 4) deliver scrubber script. EdenBank will: provide sample prompt shapes (anonymized or masked), traffic distro, and compliance constraints.
[08:33] Maya (EdenBank Security): We'll sign NDA and share the compliance doc.
[08:37] Liam (EdenBank): We'll aim to have the token distribution and sample prompts to you by 2026-11-07.
[08:45] Alex (Redwood AE): Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites for the infra kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[08:50] Ravi (EdenBank): Thanks. (background chatter)
[09:05] Speaker 2: [unclear] makes sense, thanks.

End of transcript excerpt.

Notes on verification approach:
- We'll run seeded PII probe suite (1000 items) and expect redaction recall >= 99.99% for known patterns.
- Benchmarks: steady-state 120 rps for 30 minutes, burst to 250 rps for 5 minutes x 6, long-tail stability run for 2 hours.
- Quality: automated scoring + human review for a 300 prompt sample.

Potential blockers called out:
- Customer legal needs NDA before sharing prompts (in flight).
- KMS integration lead time (ops needing keys and policy).
- Exact GPU SKU confirmation needed to finalize cost estimate.

References mentioned/links to share:
- Redwood POC benchmark template (to be attached by Alex)
- Security pack (SOC2 summary, network diagram, KMS integration notes)
- k6 synthetic load script (Priya will attach)
